A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Artemis. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison despite additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Artemis benchmark results, controlled training and reasoning ablations, and qualitative evaluations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds inference timing and V*/HR-Bench4K evaluations in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The detection reward in Eq. (11) changes from weights 0.4/0.3/0.3 for GIoU, label correctness, and F1 in v1 Appendix A.2 to equal one-third weights in v2 Appendix C.2. This is a limited change to the stated training objective; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix B.2 adds V* and HR-Bench4K evaluations targeting fine-grained visual re-examination. Existing training data and grounding, detection, counting, mathematical-diagram, and general multimodal task coverage remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 10 adds Look-back-7B as an empirical comparator, alongside Qwen2.5-VL controls. Existing benchmark comparator sets remain. Pixel Reasoner, ViGoRL, DeepEyes, and Molmo/PixMo appear in a new conceptual comparison, not an empirical evaluation against Artemis.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a timing protocol on RefCOCOg test: batch size 1, one A100 80GB GPU, skipping the first 50 samples and timing 20 random samples. The new revisit-style comparison reports benchmark scores and elapsed hours for 3B/7B models. Existing benchmark splits and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 adds an inference-efficiency analysis comparing the computational cost of structured reasoning with Perception-R1 and VLM-R1. Existing reward, reasoning-form, task-order, SFT/RL, cold-start ablations, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix B.1 newly reports five timing runs and runtime means and standard deviations in Table 9. v1 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. This addition does not establish repeated training runs or uncertainty estimates for benchmark accuracy.

E6.justification: Artemis's reported LISA accuracy changes from 78.3 to 69.8 in Table 3 and the corresponding ablations, placing structured reasoning below the unchanged no-reasoning score of 71.7. v2 also adds timing and V*/HR-Bench4K results, including Artemis scores of 76.4/67.6. The detailed MATHGLANCE subject/task results in v1 Table 4 are removed; only model averages remain in v2 Figure 3.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects Eq. (2), replacing clipping of the normalized advantage with the minimum of unclipped and clipped policy-ratio terms multiplied by the advantage, and defines the old policy. Appendix Eq. (11) also revises the mathematical detection-reward definition.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that supervising structured label-box reasoning enables a unified perception policy with transfer across tasks and domains. v2 emphasizes unification in the abstract, but this contribution already appears in v1's introduction. The introduction's general multimodal improvement claim and the conclusion remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking high matching thresholds to filtering unreliable evidence and stable RL training. It contextualizes Perception-R1 as more detection-specific and interprets the new appendix experiments as supporting efficiency and complementarity with revisit-based methods. The principal generalization interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies detection confidence scores of 1 and discarding unparsable predictions, clarifies the existing SFT/RL data and initialization controls, and documents timing hardware and procedures. Conversely, v1's explicit Rouge-1 designation becomes generic ROUGE. Dataset construction and complete task prompts are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix A/Table 8 substantially expand positioning relative to grounded reasoning: Artemis's fixed visual input and deterministic intermediate supervision are contrasted with Pixel Reasoner, ViGoRL, DeepEyes, and the previously cited Molmo/PixMo. Look-back and the new benchmark references extend this comparison empirically; several older citations are removed.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites portions of the abstract, introduction, and experimental discussion, condenses the reasoning-form analysis, and consolidates training descriptions. New appendices A–B precede the retained appendices, now C–F. Author and affiliation text changes, while the main section structure and much of the prose remain.

P2.justification: The detailed MATHGLANCE table becomes an aggregate bar chart, and three appendix tables are added for conceptual comparisons, timing, and revisit-style benchmarks. Existing figures, prompts, and tables are redistributed and renumbered, with the overall visual design retained.

improvement.justification: The corrected GRPO equation, clearer evaluation details, and added timing and grounded-reasoning comparisons improve documentation and evidence. However, v2 removes the detailed MATHGLANCE results and retains an interpretation of poor no-reasoning LISA performance despite Table 6 now showing 71.7 versus 69.8 for structured reasoning. These competing gains and losses in transparency and evidential consistency prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
